author: Michael_1973
title: On Che Guevara Road: Refugees on the frontlines against fascism
content:
South Africa has a long history of xenophobic violence. The pogroms of 2008 and 2015 are the best known, but over the last two years xenophobic has taken a more organised and more openly political form. It is now a very well organised fascist project, acting with state support and complicity.

March and March was formed in Durban in early 2025 under the leadership of Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma. It presented itself as a citizens’ organisation that only wanted the migration law enforced. In practice it made no distinction between documented and undocumented people. With the uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MKP), ActionSA and others, it led marches that included armed men while the police stood down.

A ‘deadline’ was announced for migrants to leave the country by 30 June 2026. As that date came closer, local groups went from neighbourhood to neighbourhood threatening and assaulting people and driving them from their homes. Many had their homes, property and businesses seized. Thousands were displaced.

On 18 May 2026 hundreds of refugees who had been driven from their homes went to Refugee Social Services and then to Durban Central Police Station to ask for protection. The police attacked them after which they fled to a church building where supporters of March and March and the Jacob Zuma's uMkhonto weSizwe Party tried to attack them. title: تکنولوژی و نیروی کار3
content:
REzgar Akrawi: Lo que tenemos hoy delante no es un destino técnico ineludible. Es el producto de decisiones políticas y económicas que sirven a los intereses del capital, y puede ser combatido. Ello exige una organización de izquierda, progresista y de derechos a escala mundial, trabajar por construir alternativas digitales de izquierda y progresistas, situar la infraestructura de datos bajo el interés público y la administración social, convertir los algoritmos de «cajas negras» en software de código abierto sometido a auditoría independiente, imponer la transparencia en el diseño de los modelos y en las fuentes de sus datos, apoyar alternativas digitales cooperativas propiedad de quienes las usan y de quienes trabajan en ellas, y orientar esta tecnología al servicio de las necesidades de la sociedad y de la justicia social.


Sin estos mecanismos, el llamamiento a las leyes y a la supervisión sigue siendo general e insuficiente, y la tecnología continúa rehén de un puñado de corporaciones monopolistas y de grandes potencias. En cambio, mediante la propiedad social, la rendición de cuentas social y las alternativas cooperativas, se vuelve posible arrancar la inteligencia artificial a la lógica del monopolio y del beneficio, y convertirla en propiedad colectiva y en un medio de liberación humana.

author: syndicalist
title: Barry Pateman 1951-2026
content:
Sad to report on the sudden and untimely death of Barry Pateman: anarchist, militant, Kate Sharpley archivist, writer, publisher historian and teacher.

Please find short statement from the out Kate Sharpley Library announcing his death.

"Our comrade Barry Pateman died in hospital on Tuesday 22 September 2026 after a short illness. Barry supported many other projects from the Anarchist Black Cross to the Alexander Berkman Social Club but he was at the heart of the Kate Sharpley Library for 35 years. He described himself as an ‘awkward pupil’ of anarchist history but he helped to keep it alive and made it accessible to people from new generations. We are already missing him. A longer tribute will follow. We send love to his friends, family and comrades."

[Photo from a video interview in 2011 https://kolektiva.media/w/p/paNiJusTmWE1nn2uK1RmiN? ]

author: 张皓翔
title: Here Is Rhodes: Begin the Dance of Roses!【在罗陀斯的土地上起一曲玫瑰花的舞】
content:
This book asks a question that is at once old and urgently contemporary: has class struggle become obsolete? Against both the triumphalism of “the end of history” and the moralistic complaint that the masses have grown apathetic, it proposes an analytical variable: the gravitational mechanism of association.

Through a historical sequence—from the primacy of nation in agrarian-feudal societies, to the direct class gravity of industrial capitalism, to the split gravities of the digital age (renascent nationalism at the macro level and identity-, taste-, and singularity-based bonds at the micro level)—it reinterprets feminism, environmentalism, and identity politics as displaced, uneven, yet still progressive forms of class struggle.

Engaging critically with post-Marxism, it insists that the material base and the capital-labor antagonism remain decisive. The new bonds are a genuine advance in human richness, but without reconnecting to material interest they risk becoming depoliticized enclaves.

The book argues that AI-driven mass unemployment will produce a social—not merely physiological—crisis of survival, recentering class interest while also making possible a higher unity of collective struggle and individual freedom. Here Is Rhodes: Begin the Dance of Roses! is a political intervention: partisan, predictive, and written for those who would act.

author: Fozzie
title: Answers to Review Questions chapters 26-33
content:
Answers to Review Questions chapters 26-33 of Marx's Capital volume 1. From Harry Cleaver's study guide.

1. The idyllic myth of the origins of capitalism is that it arose from some people (mostly men) saving and investing their income instead of wasting it on consumption, gradually gaining enough resources to put others to work --those who were not so frugal and crafty. The on-going propagation of the myth saw capitalism constantly renewed by the same means --by newly self-made-entrepreneurs who raised themselves by their financial bootstraps to compete with established capitalists. Thus, in Hard Times, we find Bitzer expressing impatience with "hands" who are not individually penny-pinching, self-serving and trying to climb the "ladder of success". Marx critiques these view by showing how much capitalist wealth was accumulated by theft and enslavement. Elsewhere he also points out that workers don't make enough to save even if they would, much less, save enough to invest. Nor, he might have added, did they have the time, energy, information of connections necessary to successful "entry" into competition.

title: Chapter 33: The Modern Theory of Colonialism
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to chapter 33 of Marx's Capital volume 1.

Edward Gibbon Wakefield (1796-1862), a kidnapper, ex-con and English political economist

Marx applauds the honesty of Wakefield's analysis because:

However, when approaches such as Wakefield's were tried by England in Australia:

Thus, once more, Marx concludes that the secret of primitive accumulation is:

Three interesting dimensions to Marx's analysis stand out. First, the chapter extends his previous comments on the hypocrisy of capitalist ideology of private property Wakefield's work illustrates clearly how that ideology is set aside when it becomes an obstacle to capital accumulation.(1) Second, it expands his analysis of colonialism in Chapter 31. Third, his reading of Wakefield provides a political methodology for reading other economists.

By demonstrating an acute awareness of how access to land helps people resist the labor market and wage labor, Wakefield confirms Marx's analysis in Chapter 27 of the capitalist use of expropriation. Unlike England, in Australia and in North America, there was too much land to enclose. Immigrants—both those fleeing capital's depredations in Europe and those transported as criminals—fled to unenclosed land to avoid the clutches of waged labor. author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 32: The Historical Tendency of Capitalist Accumulation
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to chapter 32 of Marx's Capital volume 1.

1. either: a) slaves, serfs, or b) private property in means of production based on the labor of its owner

2. private property in means of production of capitalism

3. social property in the means of production

This chapter sums up both the historical processes of primitive accumulation and the dynamics of capitalist development itself, especially the processes of centralization of capital and class struggle, which Marx argues will bring the overthrow of capitalism.

Marx juxtaposes capitalist private property to small-scale, personal private property in the means of production, e.g., land and tools, which he notes existed to some degree under most earlier social systems. He contemptuously condemns the capitalist ideology of private property, not only because it serves as a justification for violence and exploitation, but also because it ignores how the creation of capitalist private property involved the mass destruction of earlier forms of property.

Private property is usually justified by appealing to people’s sense that it is only proper for individuals to have property/control/possession of the fruits of their own labor. author: JournalAvant
title: In What Ways Does Capitalism Dominate? - Emma Gustavsson
content:
Editor’s Note: The author of this piece is an independent researcher and philosophy student in Stockholm, Sweden. She serves on the editorial board of Tidskriften Ordning, and works at the intersection of value-form theory, critical theory, and the history of political thought. Her personal website is www.Kommunismen.org.

A PDF of this piece can be found at the bottom of the page.

There is a conversation I seem unable to avoid. It returns at my parents’ kitchen table and in the late hours when my partner and I cannot sleep. At some point I say that it does not finally matter which of the parties forms the next government, because the social order that follows the election will be recognizably the order that preceded it. The reply is always quick and a little wounded. My partner, who disagrees with me about most things political, says that if the parties are interchangeable then politics is a fiction, and that I have talked myself into a position from which nothing can be done.

I do not think they are mistaken about what they defend. The differences between governments are real, and they are felt in places where abstraction has no purchase: in a clinic or a deportation order, in the difference between a rent that can be paid and one that cannot. author: JournalAvant
title: Anarchist-Populists & American Monarchs
content:
In the wake of the third ‘No Kings Day’ march, we provide a critique of the Communist and Anarchist Left’s tendency towards mass politics. The latter section revolves around Crimethinc’s recent call for “anti-authoritarian blocs” at the last two anti-monarchist actions.

Author’s Note: A PDF is attached at the bottom of the page.

In the wake of the third ‘No Kings Day’ march, we provide a critique of the Communist and Anarchist Left’s tendency towards mass politics. The latter section revolves around Crimethinc’s recent call for “anti-authoritarian blocs” at the last two anti-monarchist actions.

On Saturday, March 28th, millions of Americans marched to the beat of anti-monarchism. An obvious but nonetheless curious dilemma is immediately raised here: There is no American Monarch. Although we have tried our best over the centuries, God has never cast His hand to our great rulers, choosing them as our anointed national saints. No, in the name of God, our great nation has only emancipated itself further from Him in all social aspects. As such, we only have ourselves-what little is left of humanity in America-to blame for any so-called abuses of authority. In a Democratic Republic, it is not monarchy which has shown its true character.

title: ლიბერტარულ კომუნისტური პლატფორმა - OCL (1971)
content:
ცნობილი ფრანგული რევოლუციური ორგანიზაციის ფუნდამენტური ნაშრომი. ტექსტი მოკლედ მიმოიხილავს ლიბერტარულ კომუნისტურ ხედვას კლასობრივ საზოგადოებაზე, მის რევოლუციურ გარდაქმნაზე და რევოლუციური ორგანიზაციის როლზე. ნაშრომში ხაზგასმულია მშრომელთა კლასის თვითორგანიზების მნიშვნელობაზე და ბრძოლის პროცესში რევოლუციური ორგანიზაციის განსაკუთრებულ როლზე.

პლატფორმა განიხილეს და მიიღეს 1971 წლის 11 ივლისს მარსელში გამართულ შეხვედრაზე. შეხვედრა მოიწვია Mouvement Communiste Libertaire-მა[1], რომელიც დააფუძნეს ყოფილი Federation Communiste Libertaire-დან[2], Jeunesse Anarchiste Communiste-დან[3] და Union des Groupes Anarchistes-Communistes-დან[4] გამოსულმა ჯგუფებმა 1968 წლის მაისში Organization Révolutionnaire Anarchiste-ის[5] რამდენიმე ადგილობრივ ჯგუფთან შერწყმის ფარგლებში. მე აქტიურად ვმონაწილეობდი პლატფორმის საბოლოო ვერსიის განხილვაში, ჟორჟ ფონტენის[6] მონახაზის საფუძველზე. პლატფორმა გამოქვეყნდა 1971 წლის ნოემბერში გაზეთში Guerre de Classes[7], Organization Communiste Libertaire-ის[8] ორგანოში.

ინდივიდუალური და კოლექტიური ამბოხი თან სდევს კაცობრიობის ისტორიას, რომელიც ექსპლუატაციური საზოგადოებების მონაცვლეობაა. ყველა ეპოქაში მოაზროვნეები მიდიოდნენ იდეამდე, რომელსაც მათ საზოგადოებაში ეჭვი შეჰქონდა. მაგრამ საზოგადოების დაყოფა ორ ძირითად, ანტაგონისტურ კლასად ცხადად გამოჩნდა თანამედროვე კაპიტალისტურ საზოგადოებაში; კლასობრივი ბრძოლით, რომელიც კაპიტალისტური საზოგადოების ევოლუციის მამოძრავებელი ძალაა,

author: Germinal
title: როცა ამბოხი კვდება (ნაწყვეტები) – ჟილ დოვე (1999)
content:
ფრანგი სკოლის მასწავლებელი და რევოლუციონერი თეორეტიკოსი, ჟილ დოვე, აღწერს მე-20 საუკუნის რევოლუციების და კონტრრევოლუციების ციკლს. დოვე განიხილავს რევოლუციებს მარცხს, კონტრრევოლუციის საფუძვლებს, მათ ისტორიულ კავშირს და პროცესში ცდილობს რევოლუციის რეალური შინაარსის ახსნას. ნაშრომში განსაკუთრებით დიდი ნაწილი უკავია ფსევდორევოლუციური პოზიციების - დემოკრატიზმის და ანტიფაშიზმის იდეოლოგიის კრიტიკას.

კ. მარქსი და ფ. ენგელსი, წინასიტყვაობა 1882 წლის რუსული გამოცემისთვის, კომუნისტური მანიფესტი

“თუ რუსეთის რევოლუცია გახდება სიგნალი პროლეტარული რევოლუციისა დასავლეთში, ისე რომ ორივე ერთმანეთს შეავსებს, მაშინ დღევანდელი რუსეთის მიწის სათემო საკუთრება შეიძლება გადაიქცეს კომუნისტური განვითარების გამოსავალ წერტილად”

ეს პერსპექტივა არ რეალიზებულა. ევროპის პროლეტარიატმა გააცდინა შეხვედრა გამოცოცხლებულ რუსეთის გლეხურ კომუნასთან.

ბრესტ-ლიტოვსკი, პოლონეთი, 1917 წლის დეკემბერი: ბოლშევიკები ანექსიის გარეშე მშვიდობას თავაზობენ გერმანიას, რომელსაც ძველი ცარისტული იმპერიის უზარმაზარი ნაწილის ხელში ჩაგდება სურს ფინეთიდან კავკასიამდე. თუმცა 1918 წლის თებერვალში გერმანელი ჯარისკაცები, “უნიფორმიანი პროლეტარები”, დაემორჩილნენ ოფიცრებს და საბჭოთა რუსეთის წინააღმდეგ შეტევა ისე განაგრძეს, თითქოს კვლავ ცარისტულ არმიას ებრძოდნენ. მშრომელები ერთმანეთს არ დაკავშირებიან და ბოლშევიკური მემარცხენეობის მხარდაჭერილი რევოლუციური ომი შეუძლებელი აღმოჩნდა. მარტში ტროცკი იძულებული გახდა ხელი მოეწერა კაიზერის გენერლების თა

author: Germinal
title: მებრძოლი მატერიალიზმის მნიშვნელობის შესახებ - ლენინი (1922)
content:
გაზეთის - "პოდ ზნამენემ მარსკიზმა" - დაფუძნებასთან დაკავშირებული სტატია. ლენინი მიმოიხილავს მატერიალიზმის, ანტითეისტური პროპაგანდის მნიშვნელობას და იძლევა რჩევებს გამოსაყენებელ მასალებთან თუ მეთოდებთან დაკავშირებით. ის ასევე აღწერს და აკრიტიკებს რელიგიის "მეცნიერული" კრიტიკის გავრცელებულ ბურჟუაზიულ სახეს.

ჟურნალ «პოდ ზნამენემ მარკსიზმა»-ს საერთო ამოცანების შესახებ ამხ. ტროცკიმ 1 — 2 ნომრის ფურცლებზე ყველაფერი არსებითი უკვე თქვა და ჩინებულადაც თქვა. მე მინდა შევჩერდე ზოგიერთ საკითხზე, რომლებიც უფრო სრულად არკვევენ იმ მუშაობის შინაარსსა და პროგრამას, რაც ჟურნალის რედაქციამ 1 — 2 ნომრის შესავალ განცხადებაში გამოაქვეყნა.

ამ განცხადებაში ნათქვამია, რომ ყველა ისინი, ვინც ჟურნალ «პოდ ზნამენემ მარკსიზმა»-ს ირგვლივ გაერთიანდა, კომუნისტები არ არიან, მაგრამ თანამიმდევარი მატერიალისტები კი ყველანი არიანო. ჩემი აზრით, კომუნისტების ეს კავშირი არაკომუნისტებთან აუცილებლად საჭიროა და სწორად განსაზღვრავს ჟურნალის ამოცანებს. კომუნისტების (ისე როგორც საერთოდ იმ რევოლუციონერების, რომლებმაც წარმატებით ჩაატარეს დიდი რევოლუციის დასაწყისი) ერთ-ერთი ყველაზე დიდი და საშიში შეცდომა არის ის წარმოდგენა, თითქოს რევოლუცია მარტოოდენ რევოლუციონერებს შეუძლიათ მოახდინონ. პირიქით, ყოველგვარი სერიოზული რევოლუციური მუშაობის წარმატებისათვის აუცილებელია შევიგნოთ და განვახორციელოთ ის დებულება, რომ რევოლუციონერებს შეუძლიათ შეასრულონ როლი მხოლოდ როგორც ნამდვილად ცხოველმყოფელი და მოწინავე კლასის ავანგარდს. ავანგარდი მხო

author: 张皓翔
title: Double Horizons: The Logic of Exploitation in Digital Capitalism【双重视阈: 数字资本主义的剥削逻辑】
content:
When the vast web woven by algorithms shrouds our lives, when fragmented entertainment becomes the only "rest" option, and when every swipe and click we make produces value for capital for free—we in the digital age seem to have more freedom, but in reality, we are being quietly swept up in a hidden colonization. Behind the educational rat race, work alienation, and comprehensive datafication of life lies the deep control of digital capital over the entire process of labor force production, as well as the systematic appropriation of all human life time.

Based on the fundamentals of Marxist political economy, this book builds on the macro diagnosis of The Contemporary Dimension Upgrade of Capital and the foundational argument on value origin in Only One Source: On Living Labor and Value Creation. It adopts a dual analytical framework of the "exploitation chain in the work sphere" and the "exploitation chain in the life sphere" to deeply dissect the core exploitation mechanisms of digital capitalism. author: 张皓翔
title: The General‑Strike in Human Production: Geschlechtsliebe, Marriage‑Family and the Unbinding of Labour‑Power【人的生产总罢工——Geschlechtsliebe、婚姻家庭与劳动力解绑】
content:
Rooted in the Marxist‑historical‑materialist tradition, this monograph re‑examines intimate relations, marriage, family and contemporary low‑fertility crises by drawing on Engels’ theory of two kinds of production — namely the production of material means of subsistence and the production of human‑beings themselves. It introduces the German‑language analytical category Geschlechtsliebe, which integrates bodily‑sexual dimensions (sex‑drive, sexual relations) and inter‑subjective spiritual‑affective love, to break down the common conceptual confusion among desire, romance, marital contract and demographic reproduction.

The book develops a core dialectical contradiction specific to human production: the objective reality of human production versus subjective inclinations toward human production. Against this framework, modern‑era late‑marriage, low‑fertility and child‑free choices are interpreted not merely as cultural or individual‑value shifts, but as a spontaneous general strike within the sphere of human production. Such popular refusals of procreation undermine capitalism’s access to fresh labour‑power supplies, yet remain disorganised and lack conscious socialist‑political guidance, carrying risks of self‑destruction for the working class itself.

author: 张皓翔
title: Praxis‑Centred Culturalism【实践性文化主义】
content:
Based on Marxist historical materialism, this paper systematically critiques contemporary symbolic cultural theories represented by Clifford Geertz, and proposes an ontological framework of "cultural duality". It points out that there exists a theoretical overreach in the current field of cultural studies, which equates culture entirely with symbolic systems and neglects the more fundamental practical foundation of culture. The author argues that culture consists of two heterogeneous forces: first, practical culture, which refers to human beings’ active practical activities of transforming the subjective and objective worlds. It is revolutionary, progressive and fundamental, and constitutes the ontological basis of all cultures. Second, symbolic (intellectual) culture, which emerges from the need to abstract and disseminate practical experience, is a derivative and subsystem of practical culture, and is inherently conservative and lagging.

The paper further reveals the rupture and inversion of cultural duality in class society: by monopolizing symbolic systems and educational apparatuses, the ruling class places symbolic culture above practical culture, resulting in the "aphasia" of working people in the symbolic world and cultural oppression. author: 张皓翔
title: On the Illegitimacy of Fairness, Democracy, and Justice【论公平、正义、民主的非法性】
content:
This monograph undertakes a systematic theoretical demystification of the three value categories enshrined in modern society—fairness, democracy, and justice—grounded in the methodology of historical materialism. Departing from Marx and Engels’s thesis that “the ideas of the ruling class are in every epoch the ruling ideas,” the author reveals that these concepts are not transhistorical, universal values, but rather an “inverse narrative” deliberately fabricated by the ruling class in class societies to conceal the structural oppression and exploitation that they are inherently incapable of resolving. The central argument of the book is that the substantive function of fairness, democracy, and justice lies in substituting recognition for abolition and piecemeal reform for radical eradication, thereby obscuring the fundamental goal that the subjugated classes should truly pursue—liberation.

The book is organised into four chapters. Chapter One systematically establishes the theoretical basis for treating fairness, democracy, and justice as an “illegitimate narrative,” arguing that they are essentially a illusory mirror-image generated by the incurable maladies of class society.
